festivals.name: Makar Sankranti (Uttarayan)
festivals.about: The day the sun begins to move northwards, heralding the gradual increase of daylight hours. It is a time to be charitable by giving grains, clothes and money.

festivals.name: Vasant Panchmi
festivals.about: Signifies the onset of spring. For the Swaminarayan Sampraday it holds a special significance, since, on this day Bhagwan Swaminarayan presented the 'Shikshapatri' in its final form. It is also the birthday of Brahmanand Swami, Nishkulanand Swami and Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj (founder of the BAPS).

festivals.name: Republic Day
festivals.about: The day the independent nation of India adopted its constitution.

festivals.name: Shivratri
festivals.about: This is a festival in honor of Lord Shiv whose marriage to Parvati took place on this day. People observe a fast on this day and stay awake throughout the night, praying to Lord Shiv

festivals.name: Holi, Bhagatji Maharaj's Birthday
festivals.about: Celebrates the protection of Prahlad from his father, the demon-king Hiranyakashipu. Prahlad was seated in a fire with his aunt, Holika. She perished in the fire, but Prahlad survived. In the Swaminarayan Sampraday, devotees celebrate the birthday of Bhagatji Maharaj, the second spiritual successor of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.

festivals.name: Dhuleti/Pushpadolotsav

festivals.name: Jal Jhilani Ekadashi

festivals.name: Dhan Teras/Lakshmi Pujan
festivals.about: On this day, one's wealth is worshipped and prayers are offered to God for the wisdom to use one's wealth for noble and virtuous purposes only.

festivals.name: Kali Chaudash
festivals.about: Prayers are offered to protect one from the evil forces of life.

festivals.name: Diwali
festivals.about: Diwali symbolizes the victory of Good over Evil. The goddess of wealth, Lakshmiji, is worshipped on this day to receive blessings for future prosperity.

festivals.name: Annakut and Bestu Varash
festivals.about: Offering of different varieties of food to the deities. The first day of the Hindu New Year.

festivals.name: Bhai Beej
festivals.about: The day on which brothers are invited to dine at their sister's house.

festivals.name: Dev Diwali
festivals.about: Signifies the return of God after spending Chaturmas with King Bali. Today is a day to resolve to free oneself of base instincts.

festivals.about: The day the sun begins to move of daylight hours. It is a time to be charitable by giving grains, clothes and money.

festivals.name: Vasant Panchmi
